{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABcqFFOQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhGMOzA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 87, "title": "Investigate why every public animation still displays 10 seconds and make the playback range match meaningful motion", "body": "## User-visible problem

After the timeline-duration fix in [Issue #85](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/issues/85) / [PR #86](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/86), the public demo **still shows 10.00 seconds for every selected animation**. The maintainer explicitly reported that this does not meet their expectation and requests a UI playback-duration correction.

**Do not misdiagnose this as an unimplemented hardcoded max:** on current `main` (merge `19b6881610a449b5445b13ae703dc0bab9b4b394`), the initial HTML uses `max=0`, `step=any`, and `Loading…`; the runtime uses metadata/retained player duration. [PR #86](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/86) verified that **all six pinned source VMDs happen to have their last source key at frame 300 (10.0 seconds)**. Its tests include genuine 91-, 1-, and 0-frame clips, and main CI/deployment [41962115392](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/41962115392) passed. Thus a visible `10.00 s` is currently **data-derived**, not proof the UI is still hardcoded.

**Nevertheless the actual UX concern is valid:** the user wants the *useful visible animation's playback duration*, not a misleading or unnecessarily padded timeline. Diagnose the source and rendered behavior and implement an honestly specified range if the visible motion has a shorter meaningful endpoint. Do not invent a non-10-second length solely to make the display vary.

## Investigation required before choosing a fix

- [ ] Reproduce the public Uka and Gene Light UI on the **current deployed Pages commit**, with cold and warm cache, and inspect `#comparison-time` `max`, `#comparison-time-label`, current `mmdExample.duration`, selected `motion*.json` `duration`, source last-frame and retained player/reference clip duration. Distinguish a stale served bundle from up-to-date UI. Report screenshots and exact URLs/commits.
- [ ] For **all six** pinned clips, audit original VMD tracks at and near frame 300: bone, morph, display/IK, camera/light/shadow. Record per-family max frame, last nonconstant change, repeated terminal keys, tail behavior, bound/supported vs retained-but-unexecuted tracks and actual visible motion of MMD and glTF. The source audit in [docs/public-motion.md](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/public-motion.md#timeline-duration) currently says last bone frame is 0 for Uka Little Smile / Gene Happy and 300 for body clips; every source's last morph frame is 300. **Last frame != necessarily last meaningful visible change**. Do not assume the final morph key is padding without inspecting values/interpolation and rendered behavior.
- [ ] Establish whether `10.00 s` is accurately describing continuous visible movement through the endpoint, a deliberately held source pose, or misleading padding. If all six genuinely animate through frame 300, document the evidence and report that a shorter displayed duration would not be source-faithful; do not falsify values.

## Expected UI behavior and implementation scope

- [ ] Define and document the distinction between **source VMD duration** (all retained original keys; currently 10 s) and any defensible **public preview / effective active-motion playback range** (if the last interval contains no actual visible/bound changes). The normal displayed timeline should represent what the user actually intends to watch, with a clearly specified policy. Do not call a computed effective length the original VMD duration.
- [ ] If an objectively inactive padded tail is confirmed, implement a **verified, deterministic preview endpoint** based on the selected clip's executed/visible tracks (e.g. last meaningful animated bone/vertex-morph change), taking interpolation and held final values into account. Avoid arbitrary thresholds, hand-selected per-model seconds or silently truncating actually moving characters. Prefer computed build-time metadata with reproducible source evidence and independent tests over a runtime magic number. Explicitly document whether hidden/retained scene tracks affect source duration but not preview duration.
- [ ] Keep original VMD bytes, downloadable glTF, retained motion metadata, hashes, third-party attribution and unbound keys unchanged; if a separate `previewDuration` is needed, store it separately from source `duration`. Keep existing source validation and player identity checks. Do not shorten/deform the actual VMD asset to fit UI expectations.
- [ ] Ensure the **user-facing timeline max, total-duration label, seek clamp, playback end/final-pose hold, Play/Pause, Restart and Loop** all use the chosen *same* playback endpoint, while retained-source player time and reference PMX clock remain exactly synchronized. If a preview is shorter, retain an explicit way to understand/source-inspect the original duration through Details/credits (no misleading claims). Existing initial Loading… and Rest/manual behavior must remain correct.
- [ ] Include scenarios where last morph key does real work, a last key merely repeats a held value, different track types end at different frames, an unbound/camera key extends the source only, zero/fractional duration, and motion switch from long to short. No fabricated constant or source-specific model whitelist. If evidence shows active motion really lasts 10 s, do not force a shorter playback value; instead make the UI's duration provenance understandable and present the user with a concise evidence-backed outcome.
- [ ] Preserve current public 2-pane MMD/glTF rendering, Uka/Gene motion selections, all IK/Physics states and restrictions, physics replay and cancellation budgets, outline/Toon/PBR, camera, model/motion caching, audio-free player state, mobile layout, and hidden synthetic conformance harness. A UI duration change should not initialize Ammo when Physics is Off or cause extra model/texture downloads.

## Testing / acceptance

- [ ] Add tests that reproduce the reported **all-six 10-second UI** situation and pin whether it is correct or excessive, rather than only showing that a synthetic non-10 VMD is handled.
- [ ] Add at least one fixture proving genuinely animated content ending before the source's final retained key gets the *documented effective preview duration* if that policy is implemented, plus a counterexample where movement continues to frame 300 and **10.00 s is the correct value**. Verify MMD/glTF synchronized seek, final pose, loop and label.
- [ ] Maintain all #85 source-duration tests (91/1/0 frame data, exact retained-source metadata identity, fractional keyboard End/range input, Loading/Rest, real-player identity), and add appropriate real-model UI evidence. Don't weaken numeric/physics or screenshot assertions to pass.
- [ ] Verify desktop and 390px mobile; demonstrate the actual user-visible label and slider range for each selected clip and a true non-10 fixture; test failure/Retry and switching state.
- [ ] Run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, focused Playwright public-motion/body-motion/physics/UI suites, `npm run check:links`, `git diff --check`, and required sharded CI. Record actual results, failures/skips, Pages deploy SHA and browser verification.

## Done / decision gate

**Primary:** no bogus hardcoded 10-second duration remains, and the visible playback range is demonstrably derived from an explicit, correct model of the selected animation's actual intended playback interval. **If the correct interval for the six authentic VMDs is indeed 10 s, say so with source-track/visible-motion evidence; do not manufacture a different number.** If the source has an inactive tail, expose a useful shorter preview range without altering original source duration or compromising synchronization and physics.

## Repository references

- [Source duration audit and current six-clip 10 s table](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/public-motion.md#timeline-duration)
- [Public UI markup](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/index.html)
- [Public animation/viewer controller](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/main.ts)
- [VMD source and metadata audit](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/audit-public-motions.ts)
- [Existing source-duration fix #85](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/issues/85) / [merged PR #86](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/86)
- [Existing duration validation and non-10 fixtures](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/public-duration-validation.json)

## Workflow

Task for the designated implementer. The Issue author is only filing it, not writing code, opening a PR or merging. Follow the [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), prefer autonomous, reproducible checks rather than another discretionary human-approval gate. If investigation proves the UI is already correct for these assets, communicate and document the finding rather than introducing a false fix.
